page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 CPU model running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance. Network connectivity is delivered via a 200 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is a primary strength, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 21337.88 GB/sec and uncached large-block read speeds at 960.8 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 10%, with Redis achieving 359.67 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50%. Image processing and small-model LLM prompt processing represent relative performance bottlenecks, scoring in the bottom 25%.

The instance relies on the Nitro hypervisor and lacks hardware acceleration features like AVX or AMX extensions. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core count combined with a 1:8 memory-to-core ratio provides high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. This profile makes the instance suitable for large-scale database deployments, memory-intensive caching layers, software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving, while it is less optimal for workloads requiring specialized vector instructions or single-threaded execution speed.
